parsed.explanation: The combined operative regime is defined by the post-2022 exception regime: mass raids arbitrarily capture people, and documented trans women detainees went into the ordinary prison system with no gender-identity accommodation, suffering forced shaving, punishment drills and denial of HIV care — a tier-1/tier-2 state exposure (birth-sex custody with documented abuse, thin remedy, though one judge did order release after months). Societal hostility is extreme (85% finding anti-trans attack acceptable), gangs target LGBT people, and police impunity was entrenched until a single 2020 conviction. For an outed visitor — through any ID check, checkpoint or raid — custody abuse is the operative risk; no visitor-specific border exclusions are documented, and hate-crime statutes plus the conviction are modest recourses. Severe custody consequences with real capture probability sit between the 0.25 and 0.35 bands.

entry_documents.exposure: No visitor-specific border/document rule documented; the visitor's passport never touches the absent domestic LGR regime.
entry_documents.protection: Hate-crime provisions covering gender identity exist in the criminal code.
entry_documents.interaction: Any routine ID check during raids or street stops can out a visitor into the hostile custody pathway.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented: since March 2022 exception regime, trans women arbitrarily captured in mass raids are held in ordinary prisons with no gender-identity accommodation; one detainee suffered forced head-shaving, handcuffed outdoor punishment drills and denial of HIV clinic access; another remains imprisoned.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: A judge freed one detainee after ~4 months, finding the arrest unsupported — relief exists but is slow.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Prisons forbid effeminate presentation; guards, police and soldiers target gender-nonconforming people for searches, sexual assault and violence.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Hospital specialists dismiss trans patients, delay or deny care; no hormone-therapy or surgical protocols; distrust documented. Prisons explicitly hostile to gender-nonconforming inmates.
federal_state_facilities.protection: 2009 health-ministry guidelines ban LGBT discrimination in health services.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Custody-to-healthcare interaction: HIV care denied while imprisoned shows the ban is not reliably operative.

care_services.exposure: Severely restricted transition-related care; no protocols for HRT or surgery; care refusal and delays documented.
care_services.protection: 2009 anti-discrimination health guidelines and HIV/AIDS plan provisions exist on paper.
care_services.interaction: A visitor needing refills or emergency care risks dismissal and disclosure upon discovery as trans.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Documented state failure to address violence and discrimination (HRW 2020, 2021); blatant police refusal to cooperate in death investigations; police officers were the perpetrators in the documented killing.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Three officers convicted in 2020 and sentenced to 20 years each — first-ever homicide conviction for killing a trans person; 2015 enhanced hate-crime penalties (30-60 years for bias killings; 3-6 years general).
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: The exception regime's raids put police in routine, discretionary contact with anyone outed.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not specifically documented for travelling minors; the exception-regime raid/custody exposure would apply to any accompanying trans minor in principle.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Documented: ~500 anti-LGBT hate crimes 1998-2015 with many unreported; gangs physically and sexually assault, extort and forcibly recruit LGBT people; 85% of residents find attacking a trans person acceptable.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Hate-crime prosecution framework produced one landmark conviction; police otherwise documented as uncooperative.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police non-cooperation means an outed visitor assaulted in the street has no realistic recourse.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No gender-identity law or recognition; 2022 court order unimplemented as of 2023; whether the hate-crime framework has produced further convictions unsourced; no regional breakdown of hate crimes.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Constitutional chamber has ruled against gender-based discrimination (name law); judicial relief freed one detainee.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Legal challenges move slowly and outcomes are uncertain; remedies are thin against an active raid-and-custody regime.

anchor_checks.comparison: Comparable birth-sex prison placement with frequent assaults, but here embedded in an active mass-raid regime that arbitrarily captures people and adds documented degrading treatment (shaving, punishment drills, care denial). Ours is somewhat worse than the anchor.
Karthovia's pattern is police harassment with release and no lethal threat; here the state's raids channel outed trans people into abusive imprisonment for months. Ours sits below it.

Oskara features organised morality-sweep arrests with coerced statements and violence, close to the raid/custody pathway here; but this dossier documents no execution pathway for presentation and shows a working hate-crime conviction, placing it above that anchor.

Vesskar's universal biometric exposure produces verification friction without typical imprisonment; here the mass-raid pathway makes abusive custody a realistic outcome after discovery. Ours is materially lower.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime combines extreme societal hostility (85% acceptability of anti-trans attacks, gang targeting), a state that fails to protect, and — since March 2022 — an active raid-and-detention system in which outed trans women are placed in birth-sex prison facilities with documented abuse and no accommodation. That custody pathway is the heaviest input: severe (tier-1/tier-2) consequences with meaningful capture probability under indiscriminate raids, partially remedied only after months by judicial intervention. Countervailing signals — enhanced hate-crime penalties, the landmark 2020 police conviction, anti-discrimination health guidelines, rainbow crossroads — are real but thin and partially inoperative (care still denied in custody, police non-cooperation persists). The result is high risk, above the 0.25 band but well short of the criminalisation-with-execution tier: roughly 0.29.
